hints: Focus on what happens when each chloride meets water, does it simply dissolve or does it react to release acid?
Recall that $\text{SiCl}_4$ hydrolyses completely to give $\text{HCl}$, and $[\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ is small and highly charged so it releases $\text{H}^+$ easily.
Compare the charge density of $\text{Al}^{3+}$ with $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ to decide which hydrated ion is acidic enough to push pH below 5.
walkthrough:
**Sort the chlorides by type**

Think like this, covalent chlorides hydrolyse violently, while ionic chlorides usually just dissolve. $\text{SiCl}_4$ is covalent tetrahedral, $\text{AlCl}_3$ and $\text{MgCl}_2$ are ionic solids that form hydrated ions.

$$\text{SiCl}_4 \text{ (covalent)}, \quad \text{AlCl}_3 \to [\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}, \quad \text{MgCl}_2 \to [\text{Mg}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$$

**Check 1, SiCl4 gives strong acid**

$\text{SiCl}_4$ is attacked by water and fully hydrolysed to silicic acid and hydrogen chloride. $\text{HCl}$ is a strong acid, so pH falls to about 1 to 2, well below 5.

$$\text{SiCl}_4 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{Si}(\text{OH})_4 + 4\text{HCl}$$

**Check 2, AlCl3 gives a distinctly acidic solution**

The $[\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ ion has a small $\text{Al}^{3+}$ with high charge density. It polarises O-H bonds in water and releases $\text{H}^+$, giving pH around 3.

$$[\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons [\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{OH})]^{2+} + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+$$

**Check 3, MgCl2 is not acidic enough**

$\text{Mg}^{2+}$ has a lower charge and larger size than $\text{Al}^{3+}$, so $[\text{Mg}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ is only very weakly acidic. Its solution has pH about 6 to 7, not below 5.

So 1 and 2 only give pH < 5.

options.A: This suggests 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. It is tempting if you think all metal chlorides hydrolyse the same way, but $\text{MgCl}_2$ gives only a very slightly acidic to neutral solution, so including 3 makes this wrong.
options.B: This states 1 and 2 only. $\text{SiCl}_4$ produces strong $\text{HCl}$ on complete hydrolysis, and $\text{Al}^{3+}$ hydrolyses to release $\text{H}^+$ giving pH about 3. $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ does not lower pH below 5, so this combination is exactly right.
options.C: This suggests 2 and 3 only. It correctly includes $\text{AlCl}_3$ but wrongly includes $\text{MgCl}_2$ and wrongly leaves out $\text{SiCl}_4$, which is the most acidic of all due to $\text{HCl}$ formation.
options.D: This suggests 1 only. It correctly spots the violent hydrolysis of $\text{SiCl}_4$ but misses that the highly polarising $\text{Al}^{3+}$ ion also produces an acidic solution with pH less than 5.
